The session attempted a self-GRANT (GRANT SELECT ON public.employees TO analyst_ro), which would escalate analyst_ro beyond its policy (read access only via the masked employees_public view). Whether the GRANT succeeded or not (analyst_ro should lack GRANT privilege), the intent is clearly malicious privilege escalation (T1098). The remediation locks the specific Teleport principal to block re-entry, terminates any in-flight database sessions from the anomalous source IP for that role, and defensively revokes SELECT on public.employees from analyst_ro in case the GRANT did take effect. No other analyst_ro users are affected by the Teleport lock since it targets the individual principal, and the REVOKE only removes a privilege analyst_ro should never hold per policy.","language":"bash","script":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# 1. Lock the Teleport user to block all further access (24h TTL)
tctl lock \
  --user=eve.contractor@eproc.test \
  --ttl=24h \
  --message="ALRT-0004: Attempted privilege escalation via self-GRANT on public.employees from anomalous IP 10.20.7.88 outside normal hours"

# 2. Terminate any active database backends from the suspect source address
psql -U dba -h localhost -p 5432 -d procurement -c \
  "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename = 'analyst_ro' AND client_addr = '10.20.7.88'::inet;"

# 3. Defensively revoke SELECT on the base employees table from analyst_ro
#    (policy says analyst_ro may only access employees_public, never base employees)
psql -U dba -h localhost -p 5432 -d procurement -c \
  "REVOKE SELECT ON public.employees FROM analyst_ro;"

rationale: The evidence shows Teleport user eve.contractor@eproc.test, an external contractor, connected as analyst_ro at 23:40 UTC from 10.20.7.88—well outside their baseline hours (08:00–17:00) and from an IP not in their usual set. The session attempted a self-GRANT (GRANT SELECT ON public.employees TO analyst_ro), which would escalate analyst_ro beyond its policy (read access only via the masked employees_public view). Whether the GRANT succeeded or not (analyst_ro should lack GRANT privilege), the intent is clearly malicious privilege escalation (T1098). The remediation locks the specific Teleport principal to block re-entry, terminates any in-flight database sessions from the anomalous source IP for that role, and defensively revokes SELECT on public.employees from analyst_ro in case the GRANT did take effect. No other analyst_ro users are affected by the Teleport lock since it targets the individual principal, and the REVOKE only removes a privilege analyst_ro should never hold per policy.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# 1. Lock the Teleport user to block all further access (24h TTL)
tctl lock \
  --user=eve.contractor@eproc.test \
  --ttl=24h \
  --message="ALRT-0004: Attempted privilege escalation via self-GRANT on public.employees from anomalous IP 10.20.7.88 outside normal hours"

# 2. Terminate any active database backends from the suspect source address
psql -U dba -h localhost -p 5432 -d procurement -c \
  "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename = 'analyst_ro' AND client_addr = '10.20.7.88'::inet;"

# 3. Defensively revoke SELECT on the base employees table from analyst_ro
#    (policy says analyst_ro may only access employees_public, never base employees)
psql -U dba -h localhost -p 5432 -d procurement -c \
  "REVOKE SELECT ON public.employees FROM analyst_ro;"
